title: Azimuthal C/O variations in a planet-forming disk
question: How does the gas-phase elemental C/O ratio vary azimuthally in the protoplanetary disk around HD 100546, and what explains the spatial and kinematic asymmetries in CS and SO emission?

what.value: ALMA SO 7_7-6_6 and 7_8-6_7 observations and line fluxes

evidence.quote: We present a new detection of CS in HD 100546, alongside ALMA SO observations first presented in (Booth et al., 2022) (Figures 1 and 2).

recipe.goal: Calibrate, image, and extract spectra and upper limits from ACA Band 7 observations
recipe.method: Calibrate ACA visibilities with the ALMA pipeline, subtract continuum with uvcontsub, image with tCLEAN using natural weighting, generate moment 0 maps between -14.5 and 25.5 km s-1, extract spectra using 5.0" elliptical and Keplerian masks with specflux, and apply uv-plane matched filtering using DALI templates for non-detected lines.
key_parameters: cell size = 0.5", image region = 20"x20", velocity integration range = -14.5 to 25.5 km s-1, elliptical aperture radius = 5.0"
assumptions: V_LSRK = 5.7 km s-1; M_* = 2.4 M_sun for Keplerian mask

recipe.goal: Measure and validate the spatial offset of CS 7-6 emission from the host star
recipe.method: Fit a Gaussian to the CS image and deproject using disk inclination and PA; compare CS peak position against ACA continuum and C18O 3-2 reference positions; calculate beam centroid uncertainty; fit a Gaussian directly to continuum-subtracted visibilities within ±10 km s-1 of V_LSRK using CASA uvmodelfit.
key_parameters: uvmodelfit channels = ±10 km s-1 from source velocity, 20 iterations (converging after ∼8)
assumptions: Continuum and C18O 3-2 emission peaks trace the central star location within the central 0.5" pixel

recipe.goal: Construct baseline axisymmetric 2D physical-chemical disk model (C/O = 0.5)
recipe.method: Run a grid of 1728 DALI models to fit the SED for dust mass, constrain maximum gas mass from HD 56 µm and 112 µm upper limits, constrain global [C/H]gas and [O/H]gas from the CO ladder, [CI], C2H upper limits, and CO 3-2 radial profile, and fit radially varying [S/H] in dust rings using CS and SO fluxes and sulfur upper limits.
key_parameters: Table 1 fiducial parameters: R_sub=0.25 au, R_gap=1.0 au, R_cav=13 au, R_out=1000 au, R_c=50 au, M_gas=1.45e-1 M_sun, M_dust=1.12e-3 M_sun, [C/H]gas=1.0e-5, [O/H]gas=2.0e-5, t_chem=5 Myr; [S/H]=10^-9 (13-30 au) and 10^-8 (150-230 au)
assumptions: Interstellar gas-to-dust ratio ∆_g/d = 100; UMIST 06 chemical network (122 species, 1701 reactions); d = 110 pc; L_* = 36 L_sun

recipe.goal: Model azimuthal C/O variations by splicing 2D DALI models and simulating ALMA observations
recipe.method: Use output abundances from baseline C/O=0.5 model (model A) as input for shadowed model (model B) with depleted H2O, atomic O, and CO (placing removed C into neutral atomic C), evolve for 5 years, raytrace both models, splice a wedge (θ, φ) from model B into model A using a custom Python script, and generate synthetic ALMA observations with CASA simobserve and simanalyze.
key_parameters: Wedge size θ = 60 deg, wedge orientation φ = 10 deg north of west, wedge C/O = 1.5 (CO depletion factor = 0.3, O depletion factor = 0.3, H2O depletion factor = 0), chemical age = 5 years; grid of ∼570 models with θ = 10-90 deg, φ = 0-180 deg, C/O = 0.3-3.0
assumptions: Angles measured in cube plane rather than projected disk plane; shadow transit time in outer disk is ∼5 years

recipe.goal: Evaluate analytical cooling, freeze-out, and chemical conversion timescales for the shadowing hypothesis
recipe.method: Compute dust radiative cooling timescale for 1 µm silicate grains cooling from 100 K to 50 K, calculate H2O collision/freeze-out timescale onto dust grains across r = 13-300 au for ∆_g/d = 10-390, and extract chemical rebalancing timescales (for 2x CS increase and 2x SO decrease) from DALI grid cells at z/r ∼ 0.25.
key_parameters: grain radius r = 1 µm, grain density ρ = 4 g cm-3, specific heat C = 2000 J kg-1 K-1, ∆T = 50 K (100 K to 50 K), Q_rad = 0.125, dust settling factor = 100, ∆_g/d = 10-390, z/r ∼ 0.25
assumptions: Shadowing material orbits at r = 13 au (orbital period ∼30 yr, shadow transit time ∼5 yr in outer disk); optically thin regime in upper surface layers

score_reason: The ACA data reduction, imaging parameters, visibility fitting, and model parameters (Tables 1-3) are very thoroughly documented, and the raw ALMA data are public. However, full reproduction of the modelling requires the proprietary DALI code and custom splicing scripts, and exact disk inclination/PA values used for raytracing and deprojection are not explicitly stated.
